name: What Happens if Hidden Damage Is Found During Foundation Repair?

mainEntity.name: What happens if a foundation repair contractor finds hidden damage?
mainEntity.text: What happens if a foundation repair contractor finds hidden damage?

acceptedAnswer.text: Hidden damage is common in foundation work because much of the problem is below grade, inside crawl spaces, or concealed by finishes. If the contractor finds rot, framing failure, hidden cracking, failed drainage, or more widespread settlement, they should explain why the original scope is no longer enough. The best practice is to pause, document the issue with photos or measurements, and provide a revised estimate or repair plan before proceeding. In Los Angeles County, older homes and hillside properties can reveal additional complications once access is opened. Ask whether the new damage changes the structural strategy or simply adds restoration work. Transparent communication is essential so you understand whether the project is still solving the real problem.
acceptedAnswer.description: If hidden damage is found, the contractor should stop and document it, explain how it changes the repair scope, and provide a revised plan before continuing. Hidden issues may include rot, failed beams, poor drainage, or more extensive settlement than expected. In Los Angeles County, a transparent contractor should show photos and explain whether the new damage is structural or related to moisture.
